result.summary: Replaces a polling-based backoff check in feature_torcontrol.py with an explicit timestamp comparison. The mock Tor control server now records when it accepts a reconnect, allowing the test to assert that at least 0.5 seconds elapsed after disconnect even if the test thread was delayed.
result.problem: The functional test feature_torcontrol.py fails intermittently in CI because slow thread scheduling can allow bitcoind to legitimately wait its backoff period and reconnect before the test thread begins checking, causing ensure_for to fail.
evidence: Addresses open issue #36934 ('qa: Intermittent failure in feature_torcontrol.py'), which reports intermittent CI failures on NetBSD.
PR description reports the failure was reproduced on Linux by adding a 1.5-second delay and that the updated test passes with and without it.
result.changed_since_previous: No changes; the implementation remains identical to the previous version.
result.card: Fixes an intermittent test failure in feature_torcontrol.py by recording the reconnection timestamp directly on the mock Tor server instead of relying on test-thread polling. The test could fail falsely in slow CI environments (observed on NetBSD, tracked in #36934) when the node legitimately completed its backoff and reconnected before the test thread began checking. The change eliminates the race without weakening the backoff duration verification.

risk.why: A flaw would only cause test failures or false passes in the Tor control functional test.
